examples.en: Only married people, please answer this survey.
The views of married and unmarried people were quite different.
Married people are also eligible to apply.

examples.ko: 회사 서류에 기혼자인지 적는 칸이 있어요.
examples.en: The company form has a box for whether you are married.
There are quite a lot of married people on our team.
A parenting class is held for married people.

explain: 반대말은 '미혼자'예요. 설문, 서류, 통계처럼 딱딱한 글에서 많이 쓰고, 대화에서 사람에게 직접 묻을 때는 '결혼하셨어요?'라고 해요. 사람 무리를 나눌 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '미혼자'. It is mostly used in formal writing such as surveys, forms and statistics, while in conversation you ask a person directly with '결혼하셨어요?'. It is a word for sorting groups of people.

examples.ko: 친구 사이에 돈거래는 하지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better not to deal in money between friends.

examples.ko: 가족끼리도 돈거래를 하면 사이가 불편해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even among family, lending money can make things uncomfortable.
It was a cash transaction, so there's no record.
I had a money dealing with that person in the past.
I drifted apart from an old friend over a money matter.

examples.ko: 중고 거래로 모르는 사람과 돈거래할 땐 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm careful when dealing with money with strangers in secondhand sales.

explain: 사람 사이에 돈을 빌려주고 받는 일을 말해서 조심해야 한다는 느낌이 자주 있어요. 은행의 공식적인 거래는 보통 '금융 거래'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to lending and receiving money between people, and often carries a sense that you should be careful. Official bank dealings are usually called '금융 거래'.

examples.en: The two people's opinions are identical.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 동일한 색으로 세 벌 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought three of these clothes in the same color.
All students took the test under the same conditions.
Was the price the same?
Please tell me only the parts that are not the same.

examples.ko: 결과가 동일하다면 더 싼 쪽을 고르세요.
examples.en: If the results are the same, choose the cheaper one.

explain: '같다'보다 딱딱해서 문서, 시험, 설명에 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '같아요'라고 하고, 둘이 똑같이 대접받는다는 느낌을 줄 때 '동일하게'를 써요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than '같다' and appears often in documents, exams and explanations. In everyday talk you say '같아요', and '동일하게' gives a sense of being treated equally.

en: to be disregarded; to be neglected

examples.en: My opinion was completely ignored in the meeting.

examples.ko: 작은 목소리도 무시되지 않도록 잘 들어요.
examples.en: I listen carefully so even quiet voices aren't ignored.

examples.ko: 신호가 무시되면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the signal is ignored, an accident can happen.

examples.ko: 규칙이 무시되는 모습을 보고 화가 났어요.
examples.en: I got angry seeing the rules being ignored.

examples.ko: 아이의 말이 자주 무시돼서 많이 속상했어요.
examples.en: The child's words were often ignored, so they were very upset.
I feel like I'm being ignored.

explain: '무시하다'는 내가 일부러 모른 척하는 행동이고, '무시되다'는 내 말이나 의견이 그렇게 취급될 때 써요. 감정이 무거운 말이라 '무시당하다'도 많이 써요. '무시당하는 기분이에요'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 무시하다 is deliberately pretending not to notice, and 무시되다 is when your words or opinion are treated that way. It feels heavy emotionally, so 무시당하다 is also very common, as in 무시당하는 기분이에요.

en: to be equal (in rights, fair treatment)

examples.en: Before the law, all people are equal.

examples.ko: 남자와 여자는 평등한 대우를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Men and women should receive equal treatment.
I think married couples should be equal too.
Unequal rules create complaints.

examples.ko: 기회가 평등해서 누구나 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Opportunity is equal, so anyone can take the exam.
Please give every student an equal chance.

explain: '공평하다'는 나누는 방법이 치우치지 않았다는 쪽이고, '평등하다'는 사람의 권리나 지위가 같다는 느낌이에요. 그래서 '평등한 사회', '남녀 평등'처럼 사람과 사회 이야기에 써요. 반대말은 '불평등하다'예요.
explain_en: '공평하다' is about sharing without bias, while '평등하다' is about people having the same rights or standing. So it is used for people and society, as in '평등한 사회' and '남녀 평등'. The opposite is '불평등하다'.
